channel.title: The Cartographer blog
channel.description: Short, cited articles from Team Cartographer on working with coding agents, with sources.

item.title: What the research says about reviewing code you didn't write
item.description: Two studies of code review put understanding the change first. Here's what they found, and what it means when you didn't write the code.

item.title: Why a correction is the most informative prompt in a session
item.description: A correction shows the gap between what you asked and what you meant. Here's what repair research and one vendor's docs say about reading it.

item.title: Declaring done before you start: goals as a yardstick
item.description: Goal-setting research and the agile 'definition of done' agree: say what finished looks like first. Here's why that helps when an agent writes the code.

item.title: Reading your own dead ends
item.description: Abandoned branches and discarded attempts aren't waste. What research on abandoned work and recorded rationale says, and how to read your own.

item.title: Praise is not evidence: appraising an agent's work honestly
item.description: A confident summary or an 'all done' feels like proof. Two studies suggest why that's risky, and a few plain habits for appraising work honestly.

item.title: Write the spec before you delegate, to an agent or a colleague
item.description: Requirements research keeps finding incomplete requirements among the most critical problems. Here's what that means before you hand work off.

item.title: What a session transcript holds, and what it leaves out
item.description: A transcript records what was said and done, not why. Here's what research on design rationale says about the gap, and how to work with it.

item.title: Automation bias: what research says about trusting suggestions
item.description: Decades of human-factors research show people over-trust automated advice. Here's what it found, and what it means when you accept code suggestions.

item.title: What the docs say about giving a coding agent context
item.description: Anthropic's docs and one study agree on a plain idea: context for a coding agent works best when it's short, specific and checked. Here's the close reading.
